blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy
s: Diabetic retinopathy is an eye condition caused by diabetes.
It can lead to sight loss, but finding and treating it early reduces the risk.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Symptoms of diabetic retinopathy
s: Diabetic retinopathy does not usually have any symptoms at first.
It's usually found when you go to your diabetic eye screening appointments.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Symptoms of diabetic retinopathy
s: In the later stages, symptoms can include:

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Symptoms of diabetic retinopathy
s: your eyesight getting worse

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Symptoms of diabetic retinopathy
s: blurred vision

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Symptoms of diabetic retinopathy
s: dots and lines (floaters) in your vision

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Symptoms of diabetic retinopathy
s: finding it harder to see in the dark or low light

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Symptoms of diabetic retinopathy
s: The symptoms may gradually get worse over time.
It can eventually lead to sight loss.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Symptoms of diabetic retinopathy
s: Symptoms can affect one or both eyes.

s: You have diabetes and problems with your eyes or vision, such as:

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Non-urgent advice: Contact a GP, your diabetes care team or an opticians if:
s: your eyesight getting worse over time

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Non-urgent advice: Contact a GP, your diabetes care team or an opticians if:
s: floaters in your vision

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Non-urgent advice: Contact a GP, your diabetes care team or an opticians if:
s: difficulty seeing in low light

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Non-urgent advice: Contact a GP, your diabetes care team or an opticians if:
s: These symptoms do not always mean you have diabetic retinopathy, but it's important to get them checked.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Screening for diabetic retinopathy
s: Diabetic retinopathy is usually found during a diabetic eye screening appointment, which involves taking photographs of the back of your eye.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Screening for diabetic retinopathy
s: If you have diabetes and you're aged 12 or over, you'll be invited for diabetic eye screening every 1 or 2 years.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Screening for diabetic retinopathy
s: You'll also need to have regular eye tests at an opticians, to check for other eye problems that can be linked to diabetes such as glaucoma.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Screening for diabetic retinopathy
s: If you think you're due for diabetic eye screening and you have not had an invitation letter in the post, contact your GP surgery or your local eye screening service.

s: Diabetic eye screening

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Stages and types of diabetic retinopathy
s: Diabetic retinopathy develops in 3 stages.
It usually gets worse gradually, over several years.
Treatment can help stop it from progressing to the next stage.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Stages and types of diabetic retinopathy
s: Stage | What it means

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Stages and types of diabetic retinopathy
s: Background diabetic retinopathy | There are some signs of damage to blood vessels in your eye but your vision is not affected

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Stages and types of diabetic retinopathy
s: Pre-proliferative diabetic retinopathy | There are more signs of damage to blood vessels in your eye, and there's a risk that your vision will be affected in the future.
You will not need treatment yet but you'll be offered more frequent screening

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Stages and types of diabetic retinopathy
s: Proliferative diabetic retinopathy | There are more serious changes to blood vessels in your eye that could affect your vision or cause sight loss.
You'll need to see a specialist for treatment

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Stages and types of diabetic retinopathy
s: There is also a type of diabetic retinopathy called diabetic maculopathy.
In the early stages it has no symptoms and does not affect your vision.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Stages and types of diabetic retinopathy
s: In a very small number of people it progresses to an advanced stage and affects the central part of your vision.
This means you may be able to see around the edges of your vision, but not be able to read clearly.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Treatment for diabetic retinopathy
s: It's not possible to cure sight loss caused by diabetic retinopathy.
The aim of treatment is to help stop your vision from getting worse.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Treatment for diabetic retinopathy
s: If you're diagnosed with diabetic retinopathy it's important to manage your diabetes well to help stop it getting worse.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Treatment for diabetic retinopathy
s: If you have background or pre-proliferative diabetic retinopathy, you will not need treatment.
You'll be monitored at your regular eye screening appointments.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Treatment for diabetic retinopathy
s: If you have proliferative diabetic retinopathy, you'll be referred to an eye specialist for treatment.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Treatment for diabetic retinopathy
s: The main treatments are:

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Treatment for diabetic retinopathy
s: laser treatment on the blood vessels at the back of your eye (laser photocoagulation)

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Treatment for diabetic retinopathy
s: regular eye injections of a medicine called anti-VEGF, which reduces damage to blood vessels

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Treatment for diabetic retinopathy
s: an implant in your eye that gradually releases steroid medicine, to reduce swelling in your eye

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Treatment for diabetic retinopathy
s: eye surgery, such as an operation to remove scar tissue or blood from the back of your eye

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Treatment for diabetic retinopathy
s: Your specialist will advise on what treatment is best for you.
They'll explain the risks and benefits of the procedure, and what will happen.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > How to reduce your risk of diabetic retinopathy
s: Diabetic retinopathy happens when high blood glucose (sugar) damages the blood vessels in your retina, which is at the back of your eye.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > How to reduce your risk of diabetic retinopathy
s: It's more likely to happen if you've had diabetes for a long time, and if you have high blood pressure or high cholesterol.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > How to reduce your risk of diabetic retinopathy
s: If you have diabetes, you can reduce the risk of diabetic retinopathy by:

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > How to reduce your risk of diabetic retinopathy
s: managing your blood glucose as well as possible – you can learn how to do this by attending a diabetes course

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > How to reduce your risk of diabetic retinopathy
s: making healthy lifestyle changes to lower high blood pressure and high cholesterol

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > How to reduce your risk of diabetic retinopathy
s: not smoking

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > How to reduce your risk of diabetic retinopathy > Important
s: It's important to go to all of your diabetic eye screening appointments, as these can help find and treat any problems as soon as possible.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Help and support for diabetic retinopathy
s: If diabetic retinopathy affects your vision it can be difficult to live with, both practically and emotionally.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Help and support for diabetic retinopathy
s: As well as support from your diabetes team, you may find it helpful to get support from other people with diabetes or sight loss, either at a local support group or online.

blocks.path: Diabetic retinopathy > Help and support for diabetic retinopathy
s: There are also national charities that can offer support and information about diabetic retinopathy or sight loss.
